digest.component_or_area: store initialization and environment identity management
propositions: Re-cloning a tracker without carrying over git-ignored local state (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub) causes .env-id to be silently regenerated with a new UUID, invalidating all prior op-cert attestations signed under the old environment identity.

When a re-identified environment attempts to verify attestations stamped with the prior env_id, the claim gate rejects them as foreign_key because the new environment's .pub key cannot validate signatures from the old identity, and the old public key is unrecoverable.

The init ensure unit and _gen_local_files mint a fresh env_id whenever it is absent without checking whether the store already contains events written by a different environment, despite event files carrying the prior env_id at the top level.

The fix requires extracting environment identity concerns into a new module (env_identity.py), emitting a loud stderr warning when minting over a store with prior env_ids, requiring REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1 to proceed, and adding an fsck ENV_ID_MISMATCH check scoped by author.

A healthy multi-clone topology with multiple environment IDs and different authors must not trigger the fsck mismatch check, while a re-identification by the same author must be detected and reported as a store-wide issue.

Documentation must specify the four git-ignored files that must be carried over on re-clone (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub, .ensure-applied) and clarify that the guard warns rather than refuses to avoid breaking legitimate multi-clone workflows.
